traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and detailed requirements from docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md are satisfied: - Rule Naming (REQ-RULE-NAME): prefer-supports-annotation is the canonical rule name, with prefer-implements-annotation implemented as a deprecated alias in src/index.ts and validated by tests. - Optional Warning (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING): The rule emits recommendation diagnostics (messageId preferImplements) when @story + @req are detected; it is of type "suggestion" and disabled by default, so it is only active when configured as warn/error. - Auto-fix Support / Single Story Conversion / Preserve Order (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX, REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT): Implementation in prefer-implements-annotation.ts and its tests confirm that simple single-story blocks with one or multiple @req lines are converted to a single @supports line while preserving surrounding JSDoc structure. - Multi-story Detection (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT): hasMultipleStories(), MULTI_STORY_THRESHOLD, and processComment() emit cannotAutoFix and multiStoryDetected messages for mixed or multi-story patterns; tests assert both messages and reasons. - Configurable Enforcement (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY): Rule is not present in TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES, so presets leave it off; tests demonstrate that users can set severity to "warn" or "error" for both canonical and alias names. - Both Formats Valid / Backward Compatibility (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION): When the rule is disabled (default), validation-only rules still govern correctness; even when enabled, tests confirm that pure @story, pure @req, pure @supports, and certain mixed-but-incomplete patterns remain valid and unreported. - Quality Standards / Valid Output (REQ-VALID-OUTPUT): Auto-fix is conservative, bailing out for complex @story/@req lines, and generated @supports annotations are validated by the existing format and reference rules, as shown by the passing Jest suite. - Documentation: Both the rule doc and the migration guide provide migration examples, configuration snippets, and behavioral explanations aligned with the story. The targeted test run for tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts passed, reconfirming the previous full assessment. Therefore, this story is fully implemented and remains in a PASSED state despite the unchecked checkbox in the story file.
